title: The reef: one glider meets one ring

frames.time_compression: reef-world 9 tu per second; reef-contact 4.5 tu per second
frames.gif: reef-world GIF is downsized to 400 px (Lanczos), every 3rd kept frame, 64 colours; use the MP4 on a projector

view.reef-world: whole 1024^2 periodic world, 1 px per cell
view.reef-contact: 200x200-cell window at rows 452-652, cols 428-628, 4 px per cell, 0-24 tu
view.reef-lattice-detail: 160x160 cells at rows 432-592, cols 232-392 at t = 130 tu, 5 px per cell

caveats: Same P2 encounter geometry as the expedition, but in a 1024^2 world that the expedition never ran. The checked result (C052) covers contact, fusion and ignition within 3-25 tu at N256/N512; everything after 25 tu here is alm-only and unchecked by a second arithmetic route.
Ignition timing and colony mass are NUMERICALLY_FRAGILE in T and R (C053); the film shows R13, T10 only.
Not novel as a phenomenon: Chan 2019 sec. 3.5.5 lists 'detonation' among collision outcomes.
The interior lattice is frozen, not self-replicating: no division was seen (expedition report sec. 3).

runs.initial_state: REEF-field runner.build('GA', ring_shift=[64, 20], N=1024): pilot P2 geometry (head-on, b/R 0.02) from jobs-pilots.json, glider snapshot GA and S103 seeds embedded centred in a zero 1024^2 world

render.colormap: matplotlib inferno, A in [0,1] mapped linearly, nearest-neighbour
